issues.detail: The Hebrew 'מֵאוּר כַּשְׂדִּים' means 'from Ur of the Chaldeans' (a place name, Ur). The Chinese renders it as '從迦勒底人的火中' ('from the fire of the Chaldeans'), interpreting 'אוּר' as 'fire' (אוּר) rather than the city name 'Ur'. This changes the meaning from a geographic location to an element (fire), which is a substantive mistranslation of a proper place name.
